findings.title: New consent-test comment (and spec) cite payment_terms_acceptance as a live 64/512 CHECK site; the parity migration dropped those CHECKs and this same PR's request_helpers doc says so
findings.evidence: consent_integration_test.gleam:327-328: '// (refcheck rc1-1 deferred fix regression pin; same CHECK idiom as // payment_terms_acceptance and application.submitted_*.)' vs request_helpers.gleam:15-17: '//// Note: of the three original 64/512 CHECK sites, only //// `cookie_consent_log` and `application.submitted_*` still carry the //// constraints (the `payment_terms_acceptance` ones were dropped by //// the 2026-05-12 constraint-parity migration).' vs supabase/migrations/20260512182900_constraint_parity_with_staging.sql:52-53: 'ALTER TABLE payment_terms_acceptance DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS payment_terms_acceptance_ip_text_check; ALTER TABLE payment_terms_acceptance DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS payment_terms_acceptance_user_agent_check;'
findings.detail: Doc-only inconsistency introduced/reinforced by this PR's new files. Zero functional impact: the test targets cookie_consent_log (which does carry the CHECK), and PTA's columns remain bounded uniformly by the helper.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the consent-test comment (and, if editable, the frozen spec note) to reference only cookie_consent_log and application.submitted_* as live CHECK sites, matching the corrected request_helpers.gleam module comment.

findings.title: client_ip still crashes on invalid UTF-8 in X-Forwarded-For: string.trim raises badarg before slice_codepoint_bounded's decoder runs — the 'truncation, not a crash' doc contract holds only for the UA path
findings.location: server/src/request_helpers.gleam:44-45 (trim before decode); doc claim at :72-73
findings.evidence: request_helpers.gleam:44-45: 'Ok(#(first, _)) -> string.trim(first) |> slice_codepoint_bounded(64)' / 'Error(_) -> string.trim(value) |> slice_codepoint_bounded(64)'; doc: '/// - Headers are raw bytes; on a byte that is not a valid UTF-8 codepoint the decoder stops and the remainder is dropped (truncation, not a crash).' Empirically: erl -eval 'io:format("~p", [(catch string:trim(<<255,97>>))])' -> {'EXIT',{{badarg,...}}}. Old code also trimmed identically (string.slice also raised on invalid UTF-8), so this is pre-existing, not a regression.
findings.detail: A raw 0xFF byte in XFF still 500s /apply/consent before the new decoder is reached. Pre-existing (old code identical), raw-socket clients only; the fix's documented truncation guarantee is overstated for client_ip.
findings.recommended_fix: Trim/split bytes before decoding, or document that client_ip's trim path predates the decoder guarantee. Out of this PR's scope either way.

findings.title: NUL (U+0000) in a header passes slice_codepoint_bounded untouched; Postgres rejects 0x00 in text, so the write path can still 500 for raw-socket clients
findings.evidence: gleam_stdlib 0.70.0 to_utf_codepoints_loop: 'case bit_array { <<first:utf8_codepoint, rest:bytes>> -> to_utf_codepoints_loop(rest, [first, ..acc]) _ -> list.reverse(acc) }' — NUL is valid UTF-8 so it is kept; mist's header parser accepts NUL (decode_packet httph_bin verified by lens); psql verified: INSERT of E'\x00' -> ERROR: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00.
findings.detail: Same 500 class the fix exists to eliminate, triggered by NUL instead of length. Pre-existing (old string.slice also kept NUL), out of scope for a codepoint-bounds fix, browsers/proxies never send NUL.
findings.recommended_fix: Not required for this PR. If ever hardened: strip C0 control bytes (0x00-0x1F) at the header boundary before slicing.

findings.title: Doc comment 'never displayed or parsed' omits the DSAR export, which serializes submitted_ip_text/submitted_user_agent into the data subject's export
findings.evidence: request_helpers.gleam:72-73: '/// - The cut may land mid-grapheme ... Harmless — these values are stored for evidentiary/fraud comparisons, never displayed or parsed.' vs dsar_handler.gleam:378-379: '#("submitted_ip_text", json.string(app.submitted_ip_text)), #("submitted_user_agent", json.string(app.submitted_user_agent)),'
findings.detail: A dangling ZWJ or lone emoji member from a mid-grapheme cut lands in the applicant's DSAR export JSON. JSON stays valid; impact is cosmetic display of stored evidence.
findings.recommended_fix: Name the DSAR export consumer in the module comment (or accept the trade-off explicitly). Doc-only; no behavior change needed.

findings.title: XFF unit-test comment says 140 codepoints; the assertion on the same string says 150
findings.evidence: request_helpers_test.gleam:66-68: 'let xff = string.repeat(family_emoji, 20) <> ", 10.0.0.1" // 20 graphemes = 140 codepoints, over the 64-char ip_text CHECK. codepoint_length(xff) |> should.equal(150)'
findings.detail: Comment describes only the emoji portion (140); the assertion counts the full string including the 10-codepoint ', 10.0.0.1' suffix. Reads as a contradiction without that inference.
findings.recommended_fix: Amend comment: '20 graphemes = 140 codepoints, plus 10 for ", 10.0.0.1", = 150 total.'

findings.title: request_helpers header comment still enumerates only payment_handler and consent_handler ('both store the values') while the diff's own doc comments add application.submitted_*
findings.evidence: request_helpers.gleam:4-8: '//// `client_ip` and `client_user_agent` were duplicated across //// payment_handler (payment_terms_acceptance audit), consent_handler //// (cookie_consent_log audit) — both store the values for DPC //// evidentiary purposes.' vs :58-59: '/// User-Agent string truncated to 512 characters (matches the /// `cookie_consent_log.user_agent` and `application.submitted_user_agent` /// CHECK constraints).'
findings.detail: The header is a historical-origin statement (duplication story), so not false, but as a consumer map it omits application_handler — partially-updated comment.
findings.recommended_fix: Add application_handler (application.submitted_*) to the header's consumer list and reword 'both' to 'all callers'.

findings.title: GDPR test comment misstates what grapheme slicing would retain for its own 100-grapheme input (says 512 graphemes = 3584; would actually keep all 100 graphemes = 700 codepoints)
findings.evidence: gdpr_integration_test.gleam:2783-2785: '/// so 100 graphemes = 700 characters by Postgres `length()`. Grapheme /// slicing (Gleam `string.slice`) would keep 512 graphemes = 3584 /// characters past the 512 CHECK and 500 the write path;' — the pinned input is 100 graphemes, so old slicing would keep 700 codepoints, not 3584. The sibling unit-test comment states it correctly.
findings.detail: The 3584 figure is the general worst case (512 graphemes x 7 codepoints); for this test's own input the retained value would be 700 codepoints. Doc nit; the pin itself is correct.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: 'grapheme slicing would keep all 700 codepoints (100 graphemes), past the 512 CHECK'; reserve 3584 for the general case.

findings.title: Payment caller (payment_terms_acceptance) has no regression pin on stored ip_text/user_agent values
findings.evidence: payment_handler.gleam:157-158: 'let ip_text = request_helpers.client_ip(req) let user_agent = request_helpers.client_user_agent(req)' — grep for user_agent|ip_text in server/test/integration/payment_integration_test.gleam returns 0 matches; tests there only count rows.
findings.detail: P3 gap: no unit or integration test asserts the stored PTA values. Note PTA's CHECKs are dropped (no 500 risk there), so the pin would only catch a caller-side behavior revert.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: add a payment integration test posting accept-terms with an emoji-heavy UA/XFF and assert stored length(user_agent)<=512 / length(ip_text)<=64.

findings.title: XFF no-comma branch (string.split_once Error path) lacks a multi-codepoint pin
findings.evidence: request_helpers.gleam:45-47: 'Ok(#(first, _)) -> string.trim(first) |> slice_codepoint_bounded(64) Error(_) -> string.trim(value) |> slice_codepoint_bounded(64)' — all new emoji unit tests use the comma path; the Error branch is only covered by pre-existing ASCII tests that cannot distinguish codepoint from grapheme slicing.

findings.recommended_fix: Optional: add a unit test with an emoji-only x-forwarded-for (no comma) asserting exactly 64 codepoints.
